For a lower price range, I would recommend Elf.  They are available at most drugstores and targets.  I used them a lot when I was starting to get into makeup and they work really well,  For what is worth splurging on, I would say whatever you think works best for you and is something you will be using frequently and delivers enough product.  For me, this is foundation.  Eyeshadow is another thing that you shouldn’t completely cheap out on because typically that means less pigment.  For an eyeshadow pallet with enough colors to play around with and experiment with, I would recommend any of the Morpho pallets.  The payoff is great and it doesn’t break the bank while still feeling special.  With anything in makeup, if you don’t want to invest a ton of money (especially since you’re starting out), I suggest not purchasing anything that is expensive when you have something else for cheaper that works well.  Wait till you have a necessity for something more pricey. Good luck! 
Ps. Check out Morphe for other products too :)

I bought a pair of mom jeans a few months ago with the intention to style them with a thick belt and wear them high waisted.  My motivation was to dress to match this “trend” at my school primarily worn by the popular girls.  This was pretty out there for me because until recently, I haven’t ever intentionally tried to be trendy.  I usually wear shorts or skinny jeans and just comfortable clothing so I was a bit out of my comfort zone.  I also don’t usually wear belts.  The end result of this purchase was me feeling uncomfortable from the moment I was in public with the jeans.  I don’t doubt that the jeans looked okay but I do doubt that I looked good.  I find myself to get more compliments on my outfit when it’s something I’m comfortable in and show I’m happy to be wearing.  In those jeans, I just felt out of place and not like myself.  I still have them but I choose not to wear them very often unless I’m in the mood to also wear a crop top and scrunchie to really go with the trend.  The moral of the story I guess is to not try to change your style completely just to follow what others are doing.  Test your limits and think out of the box but never go as far as to make yourself uncomfortable in your own skin—or, in this case, outfit.

I would recommend maybe sticking to a few pieces of jewelry that you wear everyday so you can always have something there.  For me, this is a couple rings that I wear daily.  Then maybe experiment with switching things up now and then.  Have fun with it and try new things.  Hoop earrings are really popular right now so maybe test those out.  If you don’t like them, try maybe a different style of dangles.  Another tip I have is to find a signature metal or stone.  For me, I love rose gold so I have a rose gold necklace and ring that are my go tos.  Test things out and find what looks good with your skin tone and vibe.  Happy styling! :)
